The test image shows a close-up of stem/tissue with:
- White/cottony fluffy mycelium covering the surface
- Numerous small black round structures (likely sclerotia)
- Pale, bleached tissue underneath

This strongly suggests **White Mold** (white cottony growth + black sclerotia) or possibly **Diaporthe** (black pycnidia on stems). Let me check reference images.

## Analysis

**Test image features:**
- Dense white/cottony fibrous mycelium covering stem surface
- Numerous small black round structures (sclerotia) scattered within the mycelium
- Pale/bleached stem tissue beneath the fungal growth
- Extreme close-up of a stem — no leaf symptoms visible

**Comparison with candidates:**

| Disease | Match? | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| **White Mold** | ✅ Strong | White cottony mycelium + black sclerotia on stem = hallmark signs |
| Charcoal Rot | ❌ | Tiny microsclerotia give gray/charcoal appearance — no fluffy mycelium |
| Diaporthe | ❌ | Dark stems with linear rows of black pycnidia — no white mycelium |
| Powdery Mildew | ❌ | Powdery white growth on leaves, not stems; no sclerotia |
| Phomopsis | ❌ | Dark lesions with pycnidia on pods; no cottony growth |

**Conclusion:** The white cottony mycelium combined with developing black sclerotia on a bleached stem is the definitive sign of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum* — White Mold. The symptom description confirms: "seeds may be replaced by sclerotia... smaller, lighter, white, and cottony." The reference collage shows identical white fluffy growth on stems/pods.
